title: Atomic-Scale Investigation of Defect Formation and Phase Transformation in Ir-Deposited Ga2O3 Schottky Diodes
content: Among the different polymorphs of gallium oxide (Ga2O3), monoclinic β-Ga2O3 remains the most thermodynamically stable and is thus the preferred choice for next-generation power electronics [1]. However, its electronic and structural properties can be significantly altered by external stimuli such as metal deposition, ion implantation, and annealing, leading to defect formation, phase transformations and eventually to premature dielectric breakdown [2]. Moreover, in high-power and high-frequency applications, where devices might experience extremely high electric fields, thermal cycling, mechanical stress, and oxidation, which can interact synergistically to accelerate material degradation. Understanding the fundamental atomic-scale mechanisms governing defect formation and phase stability is essential for improving the resilience of β-Ga2O3-based devices in demanding environments.
